# Benign esophageal neoplasms

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Gastroenterology > Diseases of the esophagus > Benign esophageal neoplasms*

[Original Article Link](/library/C90qpR)

---

## Summary

Benign esophageal <u>neoplasms</u> are uncommon lesions that arise from the esophageal wall. Predominant types include esophageal <u>leiomyomas</u>, <u>gastrointestinal stromal tumors</u> (<u>GISTs</u>), squamous papillomas, and inflammatory or fibrovascular polyps. Clinical presentation varies with <u>tumor</u> type and size; patients may be asymptomatic or experience <u>dysphagia</u> and symptoms consistent with <u>gastroesophageal reflux disease</u> (<u>GERD</u>). Diagnosis typically involves endoscopic evaluation with tissue <u>biopsy</u> for histopathologic confirmation. Treatment generally consists of <u>tumor</u> resection or <u>endoscopic ablation</u>, depending on lesion characteristics and patient factors.

---

## Esophageal inflammatory polyp

### Definition [[1]](/library/PYVW6G0)




Esophageal inflammatory or <u>hyperplastic polyp</u>, also known as inflammatory pseudotumor, is a benign polypoid lesion of the <u>esophagus</u>.




### Etiology [[5]](/library/aXVQ9G0)[[8]](/library/bXVH9G0)




* <u>GERD</u>

* <u>Barrett esophagus</u>

* <u>Esophagitis</u> (e.g., medication induced, infection)

* <u>Iatrogenic</u> (e.g., polypectomy sites, <u>photodynamic therapy</u>)





### Clinical features [[5]](/library/aXVQ9G0)




* Typically asymptomatic

* Symptoms of underlying condition (e.g., <u>clinical features of GERD</u>)

* Extremely rare: symptoms of luminal obstruction or <u>GI bleed</u> if the polyp is large





### Diagnosis [[1]](/library/PYVW6G0)




The diagnosis is made based on histological findings since it is indistinguishable from other subepithelial lesions on endoscopy and <u>EUS</u>.




* <u>EGD</u> and <u>EUS</u>: homogeneous mass that is either <u>hypoechoic</u> or <u>hyperechoic</u> with indistinct margins.

* Tissue <u>biopsy</u> (confirmatory): reactive <u>fibroblasts</u> with an inflammatory infiltrate and <u>blood vessels</u>





### Management [[1]](/library/PYVW6G0)




Endoscopic resection is often a viable treatment option.
